verdict.rationale: Stripe Identity's own API documents creating verification sessions, tracking status through completion, webhook outcome events, and programmatic retrieval of extracted data with a secret key. Stripe also documents an official MCP server for the Stripe API, but no evidence shows it exposes Identity tools. Re-checks and scoped (restricted) credentials are also unevidenced; the docs mention only a full secret key. Missing for 10: documented API re-check/re-verify trigger, scoped/restricted-key credentials for Identity, evidence the MCP server covers Identity sessions, independent hands-on corroboration of agent use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can operate the verification pipeline — create sessions, poll outcomes, retrieve extracted data, and trigger re-checks through the API or an MCP surface with scoped credentials

citations.quote: This API tracks a verification, from initial creation through the entire verification process, and shows verification results upon completion.
Stripe generates events every time a session changes status.
You can access most verification details programmatically... using your secret key.
The Stripe Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides tools that AI agents can use to interact with the Stripe API
